llm_proposer.assessment: The dominant evidence is the simultaneous ~68 ps DGD increase on many channels, followed by high pre-FEC BER and OTU_LOF, while optical power, OSNR, and amplifier telemetry remained unchanged. This points to a DGD rise in a common fibre span on the S14-to-S04 optical path; the available observations do not identify which individual span.

proposals.rationale: Many independent channels show nearly identical large DGD increases at the same time, with resulting BER and frame loss but no power or OSNR change, exactly matching a shared fibre DGD rise upstream of the S04 receiver. The telemetry does not localize the fault to one of the six spans on that path.

A switch-fabric failure at S14 could interrupt the broad set of services terminating there, including protected services, while unrelated traffic remains operational. It is strongly disfavoured because it does not naturally explain the simultaneous, consistent DGD and pre-FEC BER changes on numerous optical channels.
proposals.note: site named; its node equipment does not document the mode

proposals.rationale: Physical stress or handling of the common fibre route could potentially coincide with the polarization disturbance. However, the documented effect is a brief power excursion, whereas no relevant power change was observed and the outage persisted.
